name: Exact nesting between levels
rationale: Squares (1:4) and triangles (1:4) partition the parent cell exactly; no hexagonal aperture does.

name: Usable approximate hierarchy
rationale: Hexagonal hierarchies (e.g. H3 aperture 7) cover the parent only approximately but remain usable for indexing.

name: Raster alignment
rationale: Square cells align with remote-sensing pixels and tiles without resampling.

name: Prefix geocode / space-filling curve
rationale: Morton/Hilbert interleaving gives codes whose truncation equals moving up one level.

name: Uniform neighbourhood
rationale: Hexagons have six equidistant neighbours; squares have 4 or 8 at two distances; triangles have three neighbour types.

name: Congruent cell orientation
rationale: Triangular cells alternate between up and down orientation.

name: Compactness (normalised IPQ)
rationale: IPQ = 4*pi*A/P^2: hexagon 0.907, square 0.785, triangle 0.605; normalised to the hexagon.

name: Interval subpaving
rationale: Interval arithmetic operates natively on boxes (Cartesian products of intervals), i.e. quadrilaterals.

name: Cartographic legacy compatibility
rationale: Map sheets, WMTS tiles and statistical grids (INSPIRE, IBGE) are square.
